key_insight: In the infinite-width limit, regularized Newton and Gauss–Newton training drive PINN PDE residuals to zero despite the limiting kernel having no spectral gap.
engineering_relevance: The analysis supports second-order optimization for neural PDE solvers and explains how regularization can mitigate gradient descent’s spectral bias.
method: Analyze regularized Newton and Gauss–Newton training as network width tends to infinity.
Establish convergence in probability, with explicit rates, to deterministic dynamics governed by a PDE-associated Newton neural tangent kernel.
Prove exponential residual decay on any fixed set of leading eigenfunctions when regularization is sufficiently small.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence guarantees rather than numerical benchmarks, with convergence to the PDE solution requiring mild assumptions.
watch_item: Infinite-width guarantees do not directly establish finite-network performance, and training requires solving width-dependent linear systems with potentially indefinite Newton Hessians.
paper_title: Global Convergence of Second-Order Methods for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in the Overparameterized Limit
